name: psdi-metadata
statement: PSDI's published SHACL shapes for their DCAT resource catalogue. Vendored so that validation is reproducible offline — a checker that fetches its shapes over the network at run time cannot say what it checked against, and says something different on a train.
vendored_subset: Upstream also publishes `psdi-dcat-ext.ttl` (the DCAT extension vocabulary) and `psdi-voc.ttl` (the SKOS vocabulary). Neither is vendored, because `psdi.validate()` parses the shapes graph and nothing else, and shipping a file no code opens is the carried weight this package's dependency test exists to refuse. Measured, not assumed: validating the same record with the shapes alone and with all three files gives the identical violation set — `tests/test_psdi.py::test_the_vendored_subset_is_the_whole_shapes_graph` re-measures it against the upstream copy when one is present, and skips honestly when it is not.
note: Pinned to a commit, not to `main`. The shapes are actively refined — the upstream CHANGELOG records SHACL updates on 2026-07-02, 07-15 and 07-20 — so `main` is a moving target and a conformance report against a moving target does not say what it means. To move: fetch the new commit, replace the file, update `sha256`, `bytes`, `upstream_commit` and `upstream_committed` here, and re-run the suite. `tests/test_psdi.py` fails until the digest matches the bytes.
